column2: 'Minimum 3 hours travelling time' means a literal cumulative floor on transit time across the whole route sequence. Implemented as R1.2: Min_Travel_Minutes = 180.
Origin_Point = previous working day's punch-in lat/long; if none exists, the agent waits for today's real punch-in instead of guessing a fallback. Implemented as R0.4.

google_distance is a whole-shift total, not per-leg — Haversine x 1.4 is the final primary distance method (R0.5, R3.1); google_distance is a whole-day QA signal only (GR-R11). SELF-RESOLUTION RATIONALE for OQ-19: rather than leave this gated on a live query, the whole-shift-total reading is adopted as final because it's structurally consistent with a fact the Data Normalization Agent's own doc already confirmed — task_management_taskdetails (the per-DC-visit check-in table) has exactly one timestamp per visit, with no per-visit check-out event. Since there's no confirmed per-leg boundary anywhere in the data model for a per-leg distance to even be computed against, google_distance being a shift-level aggregate is the more internally consistent reading, not just a cautious default.
column3: A live query remains good practice and is recommended as a POST-LAUNCH monitoring item (watch GR-R11's mismatch rate) rather than a pre-build gate. If it ever contradicts this reading, revisit R0.5/R3.1 — but this does not block a v1 build.

column2: No hard cap on 80km/day or 1,600km/month — both advisory/informational only. Implemented as R1.5, R1.6.
column3: Recommend flagging cost/reimbursement implications to the SE Incentive Policy owner.

column2: Model 3's alpha is derived per Node from average historical travel time. SELF-RESOLUTION RATIONALE for OQ-20 (direction + bounds): higher historical travel time at a node -> LOWER alpha (weight efficiency more), because R1.2's 180-min travel floor is structurally more likely to bind in high-travel nodes — in those nodes, minimizing wasted travel directly protects the SE's remaining visit-time budget (R1.3), so efficiency has outsized practical value there. In low-travel nodes, the floor is easy to satisfy regardless, so leaning toward priority-capture costs little. Bounds Alpha_Min=0.4 / Alpha_Max=0.8 were chosen to keep Model 3 meaningfully distinct from both Model 1 (pure priority, effectively alpha=1) and Model 2 (pure efficiency, effectively alpha=0) at every node, rather than letting alpha drift to an extreme that makes 'Balanced' redundant with one of the other two options. Global_Default_Alpha=0.6 (slightly priority-leaning) applies where a node lacks sufficient history.
column3: Direction and bounds can be revisited after a few weeks of live data if Model 3's real-world behavior doesn't match field expectations in high- or low-travel nodes — but this does not block build.
